title: Twilio Google Sheets Integration: Setup Guide (2026)
summary: Twilio Google Sheets integration syncs SMS messages with spreadsheets automatically. Configure this no-code workflow in Activepieces.
body_markdown:
## Building the Inbound SMS Log in Activepieces, Stage by Stage


In Activepieces, the listed version takes four stages, and a run costs 1 credit however many steps it has, so the free plan's **1,000 credits a month are plenty for testing** .


Each stage leaves something working: a tested Twilio trigger, one written row, mapped columns, then a published flow checked with a real text.


You only use what the connectors list: the Twilio integration has a New Incoming SMS trigger, and the Google Sheets integration has an Add Row action.


### Stage 1: Connect Twilio and test the trigger


Create a flow, choose Twilio's New Incoming SMS trigger, and open the connection dialog. You need two values from the Twilio console: Account SID and Auth Token.


Every Activepieces connection, across the 750 integrations in the open source monorepo, opens the same kind of dialog, shown here for the Drip connector, which means a change to this dialog affects all 750 integrations.


It has a connection name, a project scope, and a credential field.


Name the connection after the Twilio account, not "Twilio," or you won't know which one you picked six months from now. Leave project scope narrow so other builders can't reuse your auth token.


If the trigger shows a webhook URL, paste it into the number's messaging settings in Twilio. Then send a text and run the trigger test. Don't move on until sample data appears.


### Stages 2 and 3: Write a row, then map the fields


Before anything gets mapped, connect Google Sheets and write one row. Add the Add Row action and sign in with Google. Use a dedicated account that owns only this sheet, because the permission you grant is the real risk here.


Put headers in row one of a fresh sheet before selecting it. The action reads those headers to build its fields. Write one hardcoded test row and confirm it lands before mapping anything.


With the test row in, stage 3 is mapping fields, filtering blanks and publishing. Map the sender number, message body, and timestamp from the trigger sample into their columns.


Add a filter step ahead of the insert that stops the flow when the body is empty. Picture messages with no text otherwise leave blank rows that look like bugs later. Publish only after the sheet shows clean mapped data from the test.


### Stage 4: Test with a real message


Text the Twilio number from your own phone and watch the run history. A new row should appear, and the run should show every step as successful.


If it doesn't, the history shows which step failed and what it received. That is usually a pasted webhook URL or an expired Google sign-in.


If one of the other tools that connect these two apps is already in your company, use it.


The date-based reminder from the table has no ready-made template to find, and Activepieces doesn't need one: describe it in plain language to the built-in AI chat and it builds and publishes a runnable flow, drawing on the 750 integrations in its open source monorepo, which means you can build flows connecting to nearly any service you use.


A request like "text the customer the day before their appointment row, then mark the row sent" is a workflow no template library is likely to list, and what comes back is a published flow in your account rather than a search result, with a run history that shows each step's result the same way the one above does.
